rust_name_coverage.meaning: Name coverage only; no claim of implemented command semantics, dispatch, arity, or output parity.

limitations: This targeted parser is not a general C++ compiler or full preprocessor; it fails on unknown registration syntax and conditions.

Types and arity are inferred only from recognized field/local declarations and CommandLineParser template rules. Post-store Config normalization, filesystem checks and command semantics are outside scope.
Registration defaults are preserved as expressions; implicit T() for Option<T> does not mean assignment because set_option_default(Option<T>) is a no-op.
The null short-ID slot is overwritten too but cannot name a regular argv option; the usable short-option map omits that null key.
Empty descriptions hide options/commands from help independently of registration; print_documentation itself does not test group.disabled.
All hidden options enter both long and short maps even when disabled. Later short IDs overwrite earlier IDs, including disabled seed-weight replacing -w window.
EXTRA disables workflow-membership checks; empty hidden group membership therefore permits enabled EXTRA hidden options on all registered commands.
WITH_DNA options register independently of EXTRA. The blastn command itself is registered only under EXTRA.
The dynamic outfmt description expression is retained without rendering its field table; known nonempty stream content establishes documentation visibility.
The source baseline binary validates only its compiled feature variant; alternate variants are statically modeled, not executed.
Source documentation pads option IDs to width 25 without a separator for longer IDs; a whitespace split cannot recover those names.
Bounded oracle probing requires POSIX Python resource limits; alternate build variants are not compiled by this tool.
CLI parser acceptance is not evidence that a command/option is implemented natively in Rust.
